Hi Sam / Alex,

Thanks again for taking the discovery call this morning — appreciate the clear context on your search for an inference platform for RetailCo's personalization pipeline. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Steady-state throughput: ~250 concurrent requests/sec, average payload ~600 tokens (mostly prediction requests).
- Peak bursts up to ~1,000 req/s during promos (12–18 minute windows).
- Latency SLO: P95 < 150ms for model responses; some control-plane calls have < 100ms target.
- Data residency: US-based only; SOC 2 + audit logs required.
- Preference to avoid heavy ops overhead — team size constrained.

Initial recommendation (Verdict): Dedicated capacity looks like the best fit given predictable sustained throughput and your latency SLOs. Hosted API can work for initial POC (lower friction), but cost and burst predictability favor Dedicated for production.

What I attached: a lightweight capacity model (Redwood_capacity_model_v1.xlsx) with cost/latency sims for Hosted vs Dedicated under your traffic profile. Also attached our SOC2 evidence summary as requested.

Requested next actions:
1) Can you confirm whether the 1,000 req/s peak is traffic arriving as discrete simultaneous requests or if your frontend already batches/pools calls? This affects batching efficiency.
2) If you want, we can set up a short runbook review with our SREs to validate the latency profile against a sample workload (30–45 min).
3) Confirm timeline — are you targeting a Q2 go-live, or is this a later FY push?

I'll loop in Karthik (solutions eng) to provide details on Dedicated cluster sizing and how autoscale/burst works.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Hi Sam / Alex — looping in with more concrete sizing + performance notes based on Vanessa's model and your clarifications. TL;DR: Dedicated with autoscale + burst gives the most predictable p95 latency and unit cost for sustained 250 req/s with 1k bursts. Hosted can work for POC but will show higher variance/cost at scale.

Performance assumptions (from our internal benchmarks):
- Model class: 13B open model distilled (baseline) / 70B family (heavier)
- For 600-token avg output:
  - 13B quantized on A100-ish class: ~80–120ms per request p95 under exclusive capacity at 250 concurrent req/s with batching (batch size tuned).
  - 70B on same infra: ~220–320ms p95 (depend on KV cache hit rate).
- Burst handling: Dedicated cluster with reserved capacity + burst pool reduces cold-fallbacks; autoscale reaction time ~90–180s depending on policy.

Commit sizing guidance (starting point):
- Small Dedicated slab (4 x GPUs reserved) handles ~250 sustained req/s for 13B family with aggressive batching and KV caching.
- Add a burst pool (2 x GPUs) or configure cross-region fallback for promo windows to cover up to 1k spikes.

Items we can action this week if you want to proceed:
- Run a 2-hour load test against a staging endpoint using your traffic generator (we can host the staging on Dedicated trial).
- Share price delta between Hosted consumption and estimated monthly commit (I can draft numbers).
- Schedule SRE runbook review + integration checklist.

I've attached a short demo recording (MAP-demo-recording.mp4) showing autoscale behavior and a worksheet (same as Vanessa's) — see attachments.

If you want, Vanessa and I can join your internal mid-Apr checkpoint to present the tradeoffs.

—Karthik
